intro.title: Min Stack
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a 'Min Stack' data structure that supports standard stack operations (push, pop, top) and can also retrieve the minimum element in constant time. You will learn how to use two stacks—one for storing all values and another to track the minimum values—to efficiently maintain the minimum. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays, which act as stacks, and basic conditional logic. This exercise will help you understand how to design data structures that optimize for specific operations while keeping your code clean and efficient.
intro.usecase: The Min Stack pattern is essential in real-time systems where you need to track minimum values efficiently, such as stock trading dashboards that display the lowest price of the day while processing continuous price updates. It's also used in e-commerce carts to show the cheapest item in the cart as users add or remove products, and in gaming leaderboards to maintain the lowest score among active players. This data structure ensures O(1) time complexity for retrieving minimum values, making it ideal for performance-critical UI components like financial charts, inventory management systems, and real-time analytics panels.
